changes.summary: Imported the fourth and final Wave 2 sub-batch (task 4.5a) -- the named-risk items -- one at a time as the migration queue directed, not as a single batch. scroll_area.rs ported unmodified: pure CSS overflow/scrollbar-width styling, no document::eval, SSR-safe by construction; its SSR fallback (plain overflow CSS, browser renders native scrollbars) needs no live test since no JS is involved at any point. alert_dialog.rs: confirmed at import time (per the queue's explicit instruction) that it can and should delegate to the owned dialog primitive's shared focus-trap/Escape internals -- AlertDialogRoot's unconditional document::Script and AlertDialogContent's own inline document::eval focus-trap script (window.createFocusTrap) exactly duplicated what dialog.rs already shares via the crate's FocusTrapScript/use_focus_trap helpers, so both were replaced with those shared, target-gated (SSR-safe) helpers instead of being reimplemented. Outside-dismiss is intentionally NOT added, unlike dialog/DialogContent: a WAI-ARIA alertdialog must not be dismissible by clicking outside it, matching upstream's own omission of any outside-dismiss call. toast.rs needed two real additions: (1) dioxus_sdk_time::use_timeout is replaced with this crate's own target-aware time::sleep inside a single spawn, matching the pattern already established by context_menu.rs's long-press timer -- a toast's duration never changes after creation, so the general-purpose restart semantics of use_timeout are not needed; (2) portal.rs is imported for the first time in this crate. Reading the actual upstream source revealed portal.rs is a pure-Rust 'logical' portal implemented entirely through Dioxus's own scope/context system (relaying a VNode from one place in the component tree to another within the same virtual DOM) -- not a document::eval/DOM-based portal at all, contrary to what the Wave 3 record's finding ('only toast.rs actually needs the portal upstream') implied about its nature. It has no browser API dependency and is SSR-safe by construction, so it was ported unmodified and is safe to depend on. Real desktop pointer-capture behavior for slider is compiled (cargo check --features desktop passes) but not independently verified against a real desktop WebView in this pass, per the migration queue's own named risk for this item -- recorded here rather than assumed.

slider.rs needed pointer.rs and move_interaction.rs as supporting infrastructure. pointer.rs's global window.addEventListener('pointerdown'/'pointermove'/'pointerup'/'pointercancel', ...) document::eval script (installed lazily the first time the pointer tracker is read) is now behind this crate's established `#[cfg(any(feature = "web", feature = "desktop"))]` target-gated pattern, with an SSR-safe stub (`track_pointer_down` no-op, `pointer_position` always `None`) for the native default -- upstream called `dioxus::document::eval` unconditionally; this crate's existing local `dioxus_document as document` import alias (matching every other eval call site in this crate) is used instead. move_interaction.rs and slider.rs themselves needed no adaptation: their only DOM access (`MountedData::get_client_rect()`) runs exclusively from event/mount callbacks, never during initial render, so no additional target gating was needed, and slider.rs's own pointer-drag path is simply inert on the native default (`pointer::pointer_position` always returns `None`) while keyboard arrow-key interaction, being pure Rust, works identically on every target. Verified for native (SSR-safe default), `--features web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (compile only, wasm unit tests require a wasm test runner not available in this environment), and `--features desktop` (compiles and its pointer unit test runs natively under this feature).

Re-authored packages/adico-primitives/src/portal.rs per openspec/changes/reauthor-primitives-from-independent-spec task 3.1. No ARIA pattern applies (this is a render-composition primitive, not a widget); its spec is its one real consumer's need (toast.rs) plus the deliberate scope line the module doc comment already drew against design.md §8a's separately-tracked, unimplemented real DOM-escaping portal in build-adico-component-ecosystem -- confirmed that inventory still lists a real DOM portal as net-new/unbuilt, so this task re-authors the existing same-VDOM relay, it does not implement that separate capability. The implementation itself is unchanged (already independently structured, admitted 'ported unmodified' by its own prior header). Added 6 tests in the new packages/adico-primitives/tests/test_portal.rs (none existed previously), which surfaced a real, previously-undocumented ordering requirement: PortalOut reads its portal's content at the moment PortalOut itself renders, with no way to react to a PortalIn that runs later in the same rebuild pass, so a PortalOut declared before its matching PortalIn renders stale (initially empty) content. toast.rs, this module's only consumer, already declares PortalIn first, which is why this was never hit in practice. Documented as a caveat in the module's own doc comment rather than silently left for the next caller to trip over; not changed, since fixing it (a reactive map read) risks altering unrelated ordering-independent behavior and no consumer needs it. Verified: cargo fmt --all --check, cargo check --locked --workspace, cargo clippy --locked -p adico-cli -p adico-primitives -p adico-registry-core -p adico-test-utils -p adico-xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --locked on the same five packages (all passing), cargo run -p adico-xtask -- provenance check (44 → 43 source units, this record's file count 7 → 6). No registry facade depends on portal.rs directly (toast.rs is the only consumer, and toast's own registry facade wasn't changed).

Re-authored packages/adico-primitives/src/pointer.rs and move_interaction.rs per openspec/changes/reauthor-primitives-from-independent-spec task 3.2 (build-adico-component-ecosystem task 7.8's inventory names a 'unified press/long-press/drag' primitive as the eventual consolidation target). No ARIA pattern applies to either file; confirmed gesture.rs (the primitive that consolidation named) only unified press/long-press timers (context_menu.rs's/selectable.rs's duplicated logic) and does not cover these two files' separate concern, continuous drag-position tracking -- gesture.rs's own doc comment already says so explicitly. This task therefore re-authors pointer.rs/move_interaction.rs against their existing architecture (this crate's established `#[cfg(any(feature = "web", feature = "native"))]` target-gating around a document::eval-backed global listener), it does not merge them into gesture.rs. Inherited, rather than re-investigated, a significant finding gesture.rs's own doc comment already recorded: pointer.rs's global `window.addEventListener('pointer*', ...)` listener is installed by the same long-lived, repeatedly-firing document::eval pattern the wave3-overlays record documents as never actually registering in this Dioxus 0.7.9/0.7.10 web runtime -- if that defect applies here too (plausible, not independently re-confirmed by this task), pointer dragging on slider/color_picker does not track position on web today. Now stated directly in pointer.rs's own doc comment rather than only in a sibling file's. Ungated `Pointer`/`upsert_pointer` (pure Vec bookkeeping with no DOM dependency, artificially gated only because they sat next to genuinely target-coupled code) and widened both to `pub` so they're testable under default features -- this also surfaced that pointer.rs's one prior test never actually ran under this repo's baseline `cargo test` command at all (it was gated `#[cfg(all(test, any(feature = "web", feature = "native")))]`, and default features are `[]`), a pre-existing validation-matrix gap now closed for this file. Added 3 tests in the new packages/adico-primitives/tests/test_pointer.rs (insert, update, multi-pointer independence -- only 'update' existed before) and 10 tests in the new packages/adico-primitives/tests/test_move_interaction.rs: the file's own prior 4 keyboard-mapping tests moved unchanged, plus 6 new tests driving `MoveInteraction::start_pointer`/`pointer_move`/`end_pointer` directly through their already-fully-public API via a synthetic HasPointerData impl (mirroring the file's own prior HasKeyboardData test pattern) -- no further `pub`-for-tests widening needed on move_interaction.rs itself. `pointer_move`'s delta-computation branch only has real position data under `web`/`native` (pointer.rs's stub always returns None otherwise), so that branch has its own `#[cfg(any(feature = "web", feature = "native"))]`-gated test, verified with `cargo test -p adico-primitives --features web` and `--features native` in addition to default features (matching, and now visible from, pointer.rs's own pre-existing gating convention) -- neither is part of this repo's default `cargo test` baseline. Also fixed a latent clippy gap this investigation surfaced in tests/test_select.rs and tests/test_combobox.rs (from tasks 2.1/2.2): imports used only inside their `#[cfg(not(any(feature = "web", feature = "native")))]`-gated open_by_default submodules were declared at file scope, so `cargo clippy --features web` (not part of the default baseline either, which is why this was never caught) failed on unused-imports; moved into the gated submodules where they're actually used. Verified: cargo fmt --all --check, cargo check --locked --workspace, cargo clippy --locked -p adico-cli -p adico-primitives -p adico-registry-core -p adico-test-utils -p adico-xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo clippy -p adico-primitives --all-targets --features web -- -D warnings, --features native (both clean), cargo test --locked on the same five packages (all passing) plus cargo test -p adico-primitives --features web and --features native (all passing), cargo run -p adico-xtask -- provenance check (43 → 41 source units, -2 exact). No registry facade depends on pointer.rs/move_interaction.rs directly (slider.rs and color_picker.rs are the only consumers, neither touched by this task).

Re-authored packages/adico-primitives/src/toast.rs per openspec/changes/reauthor-primitives-from-independent-spec task 4.2. No logic changes to the timer/portal design -- this file's own prior header already documented it as a genuine adaptation (target-aware time::sleep, first import of portal.rs), not ported-unmodified, and that design was already correct, so the rewrite is spec-derivation plus a small pure-logic extraction. Derived from the WAI-ARIA APG alert pattern (each Toast is role="alertdialog" wrapping a role="alert" live region); ToastProvider's queue-manager has no APG pattern of its own, so its spec is portal.rs's already-re-authored same-VDOM relay contract (task 3.1) plus this file's own prior timer design. Extracted the max-toast eviction logic (prefer removing a non-permanent toast, fall back to the oldest if all are permanent) out of add_toast's inline while loop into a new pub fn enforce_max_toasts, and widened ToastRecord to pub, per this crate's test-placement convention -- both were the only genuinely testable pure logic in a 761-line, zero-test file otherwise built almost entirely from Signal-backed component state. Added 8 tests in the new packages/adico-primitives/tests/test_toast.rs: 4 direct enforce_max_toasts tests (previously zero coverage) plus 4 render-level tests constructing Toast's props directly inside a bare ToastProvider ancestor (ARIA alertdialog/alert roles, data-type/data-permanent/data-toast-even-odd/data-top attributes, aria-describedby only when a description is set, default close button), bypassing use_toast()/add_toast entirely. Auto-dismiss timing itself has no coverage: attempted a #[tokio::test(start_paused = true)] harness advancing virtual time past the use_effect-spawned crate::time::sleep, but even the prerequisite step -- a toast added via use_toast().info(...) from a hook or effect -- never appeared in rendered output after rebuild_in_place() plus VirtualDom::wait_for_work(), the same effect/signal-timing limitation this change has documented elsewhere (select.rs's SelectGroupLabel wiring, portal.rs's PortalIn/PortalOut ordering) but now confirmed to extend to a from-scratch async/paused-clock harness too, not just a bare rebuild_in_place(). tests/playwright/wave2-risk.spec.ts's existing 'installed Toast appears after use_toast().info(...)' test covers toast creation via a real click in a real browser but not auto-dismiss timing; that gap is carried forward, not silently dropped. Verified: cargo fmt --all --check, cargo check --locked --workspace, cargo clippy --locked -p adico-cli -p adico-primitives -p adico-registry-core -p adico-test-utils -p adico-xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --locked on the same five packages (all passing), cargo run -p adico-xtask -- provenance check (37 → 36 source units, -1 exact), cargo run -p adico-xtask -- registry validate (unaffected -- Toast's public component API and props are unchanged).

Re-authored packages/adico-primitives/src/scroll_area.rs per openspec/changes/reauthor-primitives-from-independent-spec task 4.3. No logic changes -- already independently structured. No ARIA role applies (a scrollable container is not itself a widget); its spec is pure CSS overflow/scrollbar-width composition from its own ScrollDirection/ScrollType enums, matching the 3x3 combinations the file itself already exhaustively matches on. Had zero tests; added 5 render-level tests in the new packages/adico-primitives/tests/test_scroll_area.rs covering all three ScrollType variants crossed with representative ScrollDirection values, plus the always-show-scrollbars visibility class. No pub-widening needed -- fully testable through the public ScrollAreaProps API. Verified: cargo fmt --all --check, cargo check --locked --workspace, cargo clippy --locked -p adico-cli -p adico-primitives -p adico-registry-core -p adico-test-utils -p adico-xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --locked on the same five packages (all passing), cargo run -p adico-xtask -- provenance check (36 -> 35 source units, -1 exact), cargo run -p adico-xtask -- registry validate (unaffected -- no prop API change).
